Question: Q001
Subject: Polymaker (Fiberon) as a manufacturer
Options: Keep as its own value; or merge into Polymaker
Why it matters: The estimate model reads Manufacturer as the test house (build/src/estimate/gaussian.js, the s: covariate), so merging moves every estimate that leans on a Polymaker or Fiberon observation. Kept separate until the owner rules; both spellings are vocabulary values today so nothing drifts meanwhile.

Question: Q003
Subject: Spectrum S-Flex Carbon
Options: File under TPU with carbon fibre (ruling R014); or read it as a stiff composite that is not a TPU
Why it matters: Its sheet states "the flexibility of traditional flex filament with a 20% carbon fiber reinforcement" and Shore A 90, but it publishes a tensile modulus of 2.2 GPa, a break strength of 61 MPa, an elongation of 15% and a heat deflection of 134 C. Those are not elastomer numbers: the physics windows rule out every one of them for an elastomer. Held out of the batch until the owner rules.

Question: Q004
Subject: Spectrum PLA Metal Copper, Brass and Bronze, PLA Glitter, PLA Wood, PLA Glow (9 documents)
Options: File under the existing PLA finish materials (M011 PLA Metal, M014 PLA Wood, M016 PLA Glow and their siblings); or create generic class materials beside them
Why it matters: The owner ruled on 2026-09-18 that other makers file under generic class materials rather than Bambu product rows. The database already works the other way for two of these: M008 PLA Silk carries Polymaker and eSUN grades and M024 PETG-CF carries Polymaker and Spectrum ones, so the class materials the ruling asks for already exist under Bambu names. Creating new ones would split one identity in two (D44). Nine Spectrum documents wait on this.

Question: Q005
Subject: Spectrum Greeny Pro, GreenyHT, ThermaTech PA, PET-G FX120, AquaPrint
Options: Read the polymer from a source and rule; or leave unregistered
Why it matters: Each names no polymer a material can be filed under. Greeny Pro and GreenyHT say only "biopolymer" and publish a density of 1.34 and 1.54 g/cm3 with moduli of 5.1 and 0.9 GPa. ThermaTech PA says "PA" which is a family (D44), and every value on its sheet is an injection-moulded one. PET-G FX120 calls itself a rigid elastomer and publishes 400% elongation at a density below neat PETG. AquaPrint is a water-soluble support whose polymer the sheet does not name beyond a comparison with PVA.
